title: Where the per-role argv and settings checks live
body:
**Chose:** one shared test helper, `assert_role_scope` in `tests/harness/mod.rs`, that reads the role from the pack's file name, checks the three flags, `outputStyle` and `autoMemoryEnabled`, and runs `check_settings` (moved there from `tests/loop.rs`). It is called from the existing build, checkpoint/fix/polish, merge and CI-fix stub-run tests.
**Over:** a new test that drives every role, or copying the checks into each test file.
**Because:** the four existing runs already spawn all five roles; one helper keeps the role-to-flags rule in one test place and makes `check_settings` pass on every role, as the slice asks.
**Undo:** inline the helper back into the four tests.

title: Read an interpreter's attached inline value as its script
body:
**Chose:** an interpreter's attached inline value (`python3 -cCODE`, `node --eval=CODE`) is read as the script too, the same as the word after the flag.
**Over:** reading only the next word, which leaves an attached value judged as no script at all.
**Because:** the old code already treated `--eval=` as inline, and the interpreters run an attached value as the script; reading it keeps such a call from slipping to Fine or Unsure.
**Undo:** drop the attached-value branches in `interpreter()` (`src/cli/hook.rs`).

title: The installed hook denies a heredoc script naming the forbidden verbs
body: Until this slice's hook is installed (`cargo install --path . --locked`), a Bash heredoc script whose text says `push` (e.g. `patterns.push(`) is denied by the running hook; edit with the Edit tool, or run a script file from a scratch dir.

title: How the builder's Autonomy cut is marked
body:
**Chose:** HTML-comment marker lines `<!-- builder: cut -->` and `<!-- builder: end -->`, matched on the whole trimmed line; `pack::autonomy()` drops the marker lines, `pack::builder_autonomy()` drops the marked parts too, and `AUTONOMY` became private so no pack reaches the raw file.
**Over:** a heading-based cut (naming each cut section in code) or a second asset file for the builder.
**Because:** the markers keep the cut in the one file the rule lives in, render invisibly when the file is read as markdown, and a heading list in code would miss the bullet- and step-level cuts.
**Undo:** delete the eight marker lines and point every pack back at the whole file.

title: The worker hook refuses any command naming both words of a branch upload
body: A Bash command whose text holds both "git" and "push" anywhere (a Rust `.push(` in a heredoc, or a log body mentioning both) is refused by the worker hook as a branch push; write the script or body to /tmp with Write and pass the file.

title: The slice contract's command count is pinned in tests/closeout.rs
body: tests/closeout.rs `the_slice_contracts_commands_run_on_the_fixture` counts the contract's `{factory} docs` commands: drop or add one in assets/contract-slice.md and update its count in the same change.

title: When def prints the narrowing line, and the pack's def section
body:
**Chose:** the line naming `--kind` and `--in` prints only when a body was asked for and withheld (several matches, no `--no-body`); `def --no-body` with several matches prints the locations and the trailer alone. The pack's `ctx def` section goes through the same `print::defs`, so a name defined twice now reaches a pack as locations without bodies.
**Over:** printing the narrowing line on every multi-match, `--no-body` included, or keeping bodies in the pack.
**Because:** with `--no-body` nothing was withheld, and the hook's denial runs `def --no-body`: an unconditional line would add noise to every denial of an ambiguous name. One print path keeps the pack and the CLI telling the same story.
**Undo:** drop `body &&` from `withheld` in `print::defs()`; pass a flag from `pack.rs` to keep bodies there.

title: The layout of a grep denial's ctx answer
body:
**Chose:** the denial's reason is the hint, a blank line, then `$ factory ctx refs <word>` and its output, then `$ factory ctx def <word> --no-body` and its output, searched from the cwd after the `cd`s, not from the grep's own paths.
**Over:** the outputs with no command line above them, or ctx scoped to the grep's path operands.
**Because:** the command line tells the worker which verb produced each block and how to rerun it with other flags; the slice names `here` as the base.
**Undo:** change the `format!` in `answered()` (`src/cli/hook.rs`).
